embed.alt:
The International Crane foundation is located in Baraboo, WI. It's mission is to conserve, save, and protect cranes all over the world. It has staff in every country where species live. In Baraboo, you can see all the species in one place. Each crane or pair of cranes is provided a spacious and beautiful functional habitat for public viewing. It's a great place to visit.

You can find detailed info on every crane species on their website at savingcranes.org in their Species Field Guide. It will tell you range, size and many more details for each species.

My portrait donation this year was of "Periwinkle" a Blue Crane. Blue Cranes hail from South Africa and are a lovely crane! They are suffering much loss of habitat right now. She and her mate Harold have been at ICF for a while now and are one of my favorite mated pairs to see!

record.text:
Rained out today. That's OK. I relaxed and made this short vid of the ICF to remember my 2026 visits so far. It starts with the portrait I donated, a Blue Crane, and shows one click for every species of crane in the world. They are all being conserved and protected at ICF.
#birds #ICF

The art of surface tension gliding perfected.

A night timelapse showing the movement of Four O'Clock flowers/plant during the nighttime hours. 
The flowers move around quite a bit due to nyctinasty, there was a very light breeze at times but overall very calm conditions all night. 
The Flowers unfurl in the late afternoon or evening and twist shut tightly by morning or mid-day.
They stay active through the dark hours and rest when the sun comes up.
They do this to match the schedule of night bugs and moths.

record.text:
Timelapse.

light breeze at times, overall very calm night

4 o'clock plant/flowers show movement behavior called nyctinasty. They open in the evening, stay awake and open all night for night bugs & moths then close up to "sleep" during the daylight hours.

I love this plant ❤️ I grew it from a seed.
